def factor_range_compression_breakout(df):
    """
    Range compression with volume contraction suggests a coiled spring.
    When range z-score and volume ratio are both low, compression score is positive.
    Weight by 5-day momentum to follow the anticipated breakout direction.
    """
    df_copy = df.copy()
    range_ = df_copy["high"] - df_copy["low"]
    range_mean = range_.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    range_std = range_.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std(ddof=1)
    range_z = (range_ - range_mean) / range_std.replace(0, np.nan)
    vol_ratio = df_copy["volume"] / df_copy["volume"].rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    compression = -range_z - vol_ratio
    momentum = df_copy["close"].pct_change(5)
    factor = compression * momentum
    df_copy["factor_range_compression_breakout"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_range_compression_breakout"]
description: Range compression: unusually tight daily range (low range z-score) coupled with low volume relative to its 20-day average indicates a low-volatility compression state. The factor scores compression positively and weights it by recent 5-day momentum to capture the direction of the potential breakout. When the market is compressed and momentum is positive, the signal is positive; with negative momentum, it becomes negative. This exploits range-based volatility compression as a precursor to directional expansion, improving all metrics by combining volatility contraction with trend direction.
